+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_f", [2, 4, 8])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rows", [0, 1, 32])
+def test_direct_routes_match_independent_weighted_expert_oracle(num_f, rows):
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(123)
+    hidden = torch.randn(rows, 12, generator=generator)
+    ids = torch.randint(0, 128, (rows, 8), generator=generator, dtype=torch.int32)
+    weights = torch.rand(rows, 8, generator=generator)
+    weights /= weights.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
+    if rows:
+        # Several experts on one F, a dropped route, and zero-weight routes.
+        ids[0] = torch.tensor([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, -1])
+        weights[0, -2:] = 0
+    experts = torch.randn(128, 12, 12, generator=generator)
+    expected = torch.zeros_like(hidden)
+    for token in range(rows):
+        for route in range(8):
+            expert = int(ids[token, route])
+            if expert >= 0:
+                expected[token] += weights[token, route] * (
+                    hidden[token] @ experts[expert]
+                )
+
+    x, idx, w = direct_payload(hidden, ids, weights)
+    assert x.data_ptr() == hidden.data_ptr()  # no per-F hidden packing
+    assert idx.dtype == torch.int64
+    torch.testing.assert_close(idx, ids.to(torch.int64))
+    torch.testing.assert_close(w, weights)
+    partials = []
+    seen = torch.zeros_like(ids, dtype=torch.int32)
+    for f in range(num_f):
+        # Match the native StandardDispatcher's global-to-local drop behavior.
+        local = (idx >= f * (128 // num_f)) & (idx < (f + 1) * (128 // num_f))
+        seen += local.int()
+        selected_weights = experts[idx.clamp_min(0)]
+        y = torch.einsum("rh,rkhj->rkj", x, selected_weights)
+        partials.append((y * torch.where(local, w, 0)[..., None]).sum(dim=1))
+    torch.testing.assert_close(seen, (ids >= 0).int())
+    actual = torch.empty_like(hidden)
+    before_ptr = actual.data_ptr()
+    combine_partials(torch.stack(partials), actual)
+    assert actual.data_ptr() == before_ptr
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, atol=2e-6, rtol=2e-5)
+

+def test_native_exchange_waits_for_send_before_reusing_receive_buffer(monkeypatch):

+        (torch.zeros(1, 1, 2), torch.zeros(1, 1, 8), torch.zeros(1, 1, 8))
+        for _ in range(2)
+    ]
+    plane.transport = SimpleNamespace(wait=lambda event: trace.append(("wait", event)))
+    count = [0, 0]
+
+    def exchange(stage, direction, tensors, *, send):
+        if not send:
+            event = ("recv", stage, count[stage])
+            count[stage] += 1
+        else:
+            event = ("send", stage, count[stage] - 1)
+        trace.append(event)
+        return event

+            for i, fields in enumerate(plane.buffers)
+            if fields[0].data_ptr() == hidden.data_ptr()

+"""Independent all-shard oracle for uneven A/F groups and empty F ranks."""
+
+import threading
+from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt import runtime_context
+from sglang.srt.afd.cache import make_shape
+from sglang.srt.afd.config import AFDConfig
+from sglang.srt.afd.contracts import AFDRole
+from sglang.srt.afd.model_adapters import base
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=10, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("a,f", [(20, 32), (3, 4), (4, 4), (24, 4)])
+def test_all_expert_shards_contribute_and_return_each_source_row_once(
+    monkeypatch, a, f
+):
+    rows = tuple((i % 4, (i + 2) % 4) for i in range(a))
+    config = AFDConfig(lanes=f, attention_lanes=a)
+    shapes = [
+        make_shape(
+            lane=j,
+            lane_rows=rows,
+            hidden_size=4,
+            dtype="bfloat16",
+            config=config,
+            capture_sizes=(4,),
+        )
+        for j in range(f)
+    ]
+    inputs = [
+        [
+            torch.arange(n * 4, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(n, 4) + 10 * i + stage
+            for stage, n in enumerate(vector)
+        ]
+        for i, vector in enumerate(rows)
+    ]
+    barrier = threading.Barrier(f, timeout=10)
+    values, calls = [None] * f, []
+    state = threading.local()
+
+    class Group:
+        def __init__(self, rank):
+            self.rank_in_group = rank
+            self.step = 0
+
+        def collect(self, tensor, *, reduce=False):
+            values[self.rank_in_group] = tensor
+            barrier.wait()
+            result = torch.stack(values).sum(0) if reduce else torch.cat(values)
+            # Finish reading every rank before the next collective overwrites slots.
+            barrier.wait()
+            return result
+
+        def all_gatherv(self, local, sizes):
+            assert local.shape == (sizes[self.rank_in_group], 4)
+            return [self.collect(local)]
+
+        def reduce_scatterv(self, partial, sizes):
+            result = self.collect(partial, reduce=True).narrow(
+                0, sum(sizes[: self.rank_in_group]), sizes[self.rank_in_group]
+            )
+            self.step += 1
+            return result
+
+    class Forward:
+        @contextmanager
+        def scoped(self, **kwargs):
+            assert kwargs == {"mlp_reduce_scatter": True}
+            yield
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        base, "get_parallel", lambda: SimpleNamespace(tp_group=state.group)
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(runtime_context, "get_forward", lambda: Forward())
+
+    def run(rank):
+        state.group = Group(rank)
+        shape = shapes[rank]
+        capacities = shape.group_bucket_rows(ffn_ordinal=rank)
+        buffers = tuple(torch.empty(n, 4) for n in capacities)
+        adapter = object.__new__(base.AFDDecoderAdapter)
+        adapter.role = AFDRole.FFN
+
+        def compute(x, batch):
+            calls.append((rank, state.group.step))
+            # Each rank owns a distinct expert selected by global row ID.
+            chosen = torch.arange(x.shape[0]) % f == rank
+            return x * chosen[:, None] * (rank + 1)
+
+        adapter.inner = SimpleNamespace(
+            layers=[SimpleNamespace(compute_ffn_output=compute)]
+        )
+        descriptor = SimpleNamespace(stage_rows=lambda *, lane: rows[lane])
+        stages, views = adapter.make_ffn_stages(
+            descriptor=descriptor, buffers=buffers, lane=rank, shape=shape
+        )
+        group = shape.group_lanes(ffn_ordinal=rank)
+        for stage in range(2):
+            for tensor, lane in zip(views[stage], group):
+                tensor.copy_(inputs[lane][stage])
+        return [
+            adapter.local_compute(
+                layer=0, stage=stage, hidden_states=view, residual=None
+            )[0]
+            for stage, view in zip(stages, views)
+        ]
+
+    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=f) as executor:
+        outputs = list(executor.map(run, range(f)))
+    assert sorted(calls) == [(j, s) for j in range(f) for s in range(2)]
+    for stage in range(2):
+        # Independent serial oracle in global A row order, including bucket gaps.
+        packed = torch.cat(
+            [
+                torch.nn.functional.pad(inputs[i][stage], (0, 0, 0, 4 - rows[i][stage]))
+                for i in range(a)
+            ]
+        )
+        oracle = packed * (torch.arange(a * 4) % f + 1)[:, None]
+        for rank, shape in enumerate(shapes):
+            lanes = shape.group_lanes(ffn_ordinal=rank)
+            assert len(outputs[rank][stage]) == len(lanes)
+            for output, lane in zip(outputs[rank][stage], lanes):
+                torch.testing.assert_close(
+                    output, oracle[lane * 4 : lane * 4 + rows[lane][stage]]
+                )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v", "-x"]))

+def _store_transports(a, f, *, timeout=3):
+    topology = AFDPairedTopology.paired(lanes=f, attention_lanes=a)
+    store = torch.distributed.HashStore()
+    store.set_timeout(timedelta(seconds=timeout))
+    transports = []
+    for endpoint in topology.endpoints:
+        rank = endpoint.coordination_rank
+        transport = object.__new__(AFDPairedP2PTransport)
+        transport.role, transport._closed = endpoint.role, False
+        peers = topology.peers(role=endpoint.role, ordinal=endpoint.ordinal)
+        transport._peer_coordination_ranks = tuple(p.coordination_rank for p in peers)
+        transport._control_upstream = 0 if rank < f and not peers else None
+        transport._control_followers = (
+            tuple(
+                j for j in range(f) if not topology.attention_lane_group(ffn_ordinal=j)
+            )
+            if rank == 0
+            else ()
+        )
+        transport._control = _AFDControlChannels(
+            StatelessProcessGroup(rank=rank, world_size=a + f, store=store)
+        )
+        transport._forked_streams, transport._stats = [], {"steps": 0}
+        transport._peer_close_usage = None
+        transport._close_exchange = transport._close_exchange_error = None
+        transport._idle_timeout_seconds = transport._close_timeout_seconds = timeout
+        transports.append(transport)
+    return topology, transports
+

+def _store_descriptor(a, kind, step_id=0, **overrides):
+    fields = dict(
+        kind=kind,
+        step_id=step_id,
+        lane_stage_rows=((1, 1),) * a,
+        hidden_size=4,
+        dtype="bfloat16",
+        num_layers=2,
+        graph_eligible=True,
+    )
+    fields.update(overrides)

+def test_control_lifecycle_uses_real_store_with_separate_wire_metadata(a, f):
+    topology, transports = _store_transports(a, f)
+    topology.validate()
+    groups = [topology.attention_lane_group(ffn_ordinal=j) for j in range(f)]
+    assert tuple(i for group in groups for i in group) == tuple(range(a))
+    assert max(map(len, groups)) - min(map(len, groups)) <= 1
+    assert topology.pair_world_size == (a + f if a % f else 1 + a // f)
+    wire_stores = {}
+    wire_groups = []
+    for endpoint in topology.endpoints:
+        ordinal = topology.group_ordinal(role=endpoint.role, ordinal=endpoint.ordinal)
+        store = wire_stores.setdefault(ordinal, torch.distributed.HashStore())
+        store.set_timeout(timedelta(seconds=3))
+        wire_groups.append(
+            StatelessProcessGroup(
+                rank=endpoint.transport_rank,
+                world_size=topology.pair_world_size,
+                store=store,
+            )
+        )
+
+    def data_boundary(rank, kind, step_id):
+        replies = wire_groups[rank].all_gather_obj((rank, kind, step_id))
+        assert len(replies) == topology.pair_world_size
+        assert all(reply[1:] == (kind, step_id) for reply in replies)
+        assert len({reply[0] for reply in replies}) == topology.pair_world_size
+
+    def run(rank):
+        transport = transports[rank]
+        for step_id in (0, 1):
+            expected = _store_descriptor(a, "CAPTURE", step_id)
+            descriptor = transport.begin_step(expected if rank >= f else None)
+            assert descriptor == expected
+            data_boundary(rank, "CAPTURE", step_id)
+        if rank < f:
+            assert transport.begin_step(None).kind == "READY"
+        transport.capture_ready()
+        descriptor = transport.begin_step(
+            _store_descriptor(a, "STEP", 2) if rank >= f else None
+        )
+        assert (descriptor.kind, descriptor.step_id) == ("STEP", 2)
+        data_boundary(rank, "STEP", 2)
+        if rank < f:
+            assert transport.begin_step(None).kind == "CLOSE"
+        result = transport.exchange_close(usage={"rank": rank})
+        assert transport.exchange_close(usage={}) == result
+        return result
+
+    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=a + f) as pool:
+        results = list(pool.map(run, range(a + f)))
+    followers = transports[0]._control_followers
+    if followers:
+        assert all(results[j] == {"rank": f} for j in followers)
+        assert results[f]["control_followers"] == {
+            str(rank): {"rank": rank} for rank in followers
+        }
+    for j in range(f):
+        group = topology.attention_lane_group(ffn_ordinal=j)
+        if group:
+            assert results[j] == {"rank": f + group[0]}
+            assert all(results[f + i]["rank"] == j for i in group)
+    assert all(transport._stats["steps"] == 5 for transport in transports[:f])

+    weight = torch.zeros((2, 3, k), dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    # Check padding bytes are ignored when K needs fewer than four exponents.
+    count = max(4, k // 128)
+    exponents = torch.arange(2 * 3 * count, dtype=torch.uint8).reshape(2, 3, count)
+    scale = exponents.view(torch.int32)
+    before = weight.view(torch.uint8).clone()
+    actual = _mega_moe_kernel_scale(weight, scale)
+    expected = torch.stack([exponents[..., j // 4] for j in range(k // 32)], dim=-1)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual.contiguous().view(torch.uint8), expected)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(weight.view(torch.uint8), before)
+    assert actual.mT.is_contiguous()
+    assert _mega_moe_kernel_scale(weight.to(torch.bfloat16), scale) is scale

+                    return nullcontext()
+
+            attention = Attention()
+            attention.offset = index + 1
+            layer = SimpleNamespace(
+                attn_boundary=attn_stage,
+                ffn_boundary=ffn_stage,
+                self_attn=attention,
+                _resolve_gfx95_quant_format=lambda: "",
+            )
+            layer.forward_attention_for_afd = MethodType(
+                model_type.forward_attention_for_afd, layer
+            )
+            layers.append(layer)
+        adapter.inner = SimpleNamespace(layers=layers)
+        batch = ForwardBatch(
+            forward_mode=ForwardMode.DECODE,
+            batch_size=rows,
+            input_ids=torch.arange(rows),
+            positions=torch.arange(rows),
+            req_pool_indices=torch.arange(rows),
+            seq_lens=torch.ones(rows, dtype=torch.int32),
+            seq_lens_sum=rows,
+            out_cache_loc=torch.arange(rows),
+        )
+        initial = torch.arange(rows * 4, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(rows, 4)
+        stages = adapter.split_step(
+            hidden_states=initial,
+            residual=None,
+            positions=batch.positions,
+            forward_batch=batch,
+            stages=2,
+        )
+        adapter._step_id = 1
+        adapter._stage_states = {
+            i: SimpleNamespace(zero_allocator=None) for i in range(2)
+        }
+        # Reuse the same stage batches as capture warmup does, with new inputs.
+        for shift in (0, 17):
+            for stage in stages:
+                stage.hidden_states = (
+                    initial[stage.token_start : stage.token_stop] + shift
+                )
+                stage.residual = None
+            for index in range(2):
+                for stage in stages:
+                    h, r = adapter.local_compute(
+                        layer=index,
+                        stage=stage,
+                        hidden_states=stage.hidden_states,
+                        residual=stage.residual,
+                    )
+                    stage.hidden_states, stage.residual = adapter.finish_layer(
+                        layer=index, stage=stage, ffn_output=h * 0.75, residual=r
+                    )
+                if index == 0:
+                    assert (
+                        stages[0].forward_batch.residual_stream
+                        is not stages[1].forward_batch.residual_stream
+                    )
+                else:
+                    assert all(s.forward_batch.residual_stream is None for s in stages)
+            h, r = adapter.join_step(stages=stages)
+            actual = Norm()(h, r)[0]
+            expected = initial + shift
+            for offset in (1, 2):
+                expected = 2.5 * (3 * expected + offset)
+            torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected * 2)
+        assert batch.residual_stream is None
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("mode", ["auto", "direct", "fixed", "legacy_false"])
+def test_qwen_constructor_retains_router_without_native_expert_collectives(
+    monkeypatch, mode
+):
+    from sglang.srt.afd import model_hooks
+    from sglang.srt.afd.config import AFDConfig
+    from sglang.srt.layers.layer_boundary.factories import layer_stack
+    from sglang.srt.models import qwen3_moe
+    from sglang.test.boundary_fixtures import Norm, parallel_of, planning
+
+    class Router(torch.nn.Module):
+        def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
+            super().__init__()
+
+        def route(self, hidden_states):
+            return hidden_states
+
+    afd_config = (
+        AFDConfig(experimental_direct=False)
+        if mode == "legacy_false"
+        else AFDConfig(ffn_backend=mode)
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        model_hooks,
+        "get_server_args",
+        lambda: SimpleNamespace(afd_config=afd_config, moe_a2a_backend="none"),
+    )
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(qwen3_moe, "afd_execution_mode", lambda: "attention")
+    monkeypatch.setattr(qwen3_moe, "Qwen3AFDRouter", Router)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(qwen3_moe, "get_rope_config", lambda cfg: (10000, None))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(qwen3_moe, "Qwen3MoeAttention", lambda **kw: SimpleNamespace())
+    monkeypatch.setattr(qwen3_moe, "RMSNorm", lambda *a, **kw: Norm())
+    config = SimpleNamespace(
+        hidden_size=4,
+        num_attention_heads=1,
+        num_key_value_heads=1,
+        rms_norm_eps=1e-6,
+        attention_bias=False,
+    )
+    with planning(parallel_of(attn_dp=8, attn_tp=1)), layer_stack():
+        layer = qwen3_moe.Qwen3MoeDecoderLayer(config, 0)
+    assert layer.ffn_boundary.declaration.dense_tp_size == 1
+    assert not layer.ffn_boundary.declaration.sparse
+    assert layer.is_layer_sparse
+    assert isinstance(layer.mlp, Router) == (mode in ("auto", "direct"))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))

Both are part of our team’s AFD work. Thanks for evaluating these components and reporting comparable throughput through your plugin interface.

We’d welcome you and anyone else interested in AFD to join the discussion in our [[RFC and roadmap](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/45568)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/45568) or [[implementation PR](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45562)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45562). Feedback, ideas, and code contributions are all welcome.

> I noticed that this PR now integrates the MegaMoE/M2N backend from our AFD implementation in [[#45562](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45562)](#45562), together with our M2N implementation in [[DeepGEMM #110](https://github.com/sgl-project/DeepGEMM/pull/110)]([sgl-project/DeepGEMM#110](https://github.com/sgl-project/DeepGEMM/pull/110)). Both are part of our team’s AFD work. Thanks for evaluating these components and reporting comparable throughput through your plugin interface.
> 
> We’d welcome you and anyone else interested in AFD to join the discussion in our [[RFC and roadmap](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/45568)](#45568) or [[implementation PR](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45562)](#45562). Feedback, ideas, and code contributions are all welcome.

Thanks for sharing your team’s work. Our PR already acknowledges [#45562](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45562) and the underlying M2N implementation in [DeepGEMM #110](https://github.com/sgl-project/DeepGEMM/pull/110), with source attribution included in the relevant code.

This integration is experimental: our goal is to evaluate these components through our AFD plugin interface and compare performance under aligned configurations. Our earlier PR [#41646](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41646) explored integration with SGLang’s native scheduling, multi-lane execution, and coordinated CUDA graphs.

We’re now emphasizing pluggable FFN backends and communication interfaces to accommodate more hardware vendors and explore heterogeneous A/F deployments. We’re also using SGLang Simulator and roofline analysis to search for promising hardware and execution configurations, alongside further DeepEP and MegaMoE integration approaches.

We’d be very happy to collaborate and join the discussion, particularly on communication interfaces and execution backend design. Our testing has also identified performance bottlenecks in both AFD implementations and the MegaMoE paths; joint profiling and optimization would be a valuable opportunity to move these efforts forward together.
